name: Kukke Sri Subramanya Temple
deity: Subramanya (Kartikeya) as lord of the serpents, worshipped together with Vasuki, king of snakes
tradition: Kaumaram, the worship of Subramanya (Kartikeya) within the Shaiva tradition; a premier serpent shrine
period: An ancient serpent-shrine of the Western Ghats on the Kumaradhara, foremost for the relief of the sarpa dosha
summary: In a forested valley of the Western Ghats, Subramanya is worshipped as the lord of serpents, sheltering Vasuki the snake-king beneath him. Pilgrims come from across India to seek relief from the sarpa dosha at what is held the foremost of serpent shrines.

sections.history: Kukke Subramanya stands in a green valley of the Western Ghats, on the banks of the Kumaradhara in Dakshina Kannada. It is among the most revered temples of coastal Karnataka and the foremost shrine in the land for the worship of the serpent, where Subramanya — Kartikeya, the warrior son of Shiva — is honoured together with Vasuki, the king of snakes. For centuries pilgrims have come here above all to perform the rites that relieve the sarpa dosha, the affliction traditionally traced to a wrong done to serpents.
sections.architecture: The temple sits in the Dravidian manner of the Tulunadu country, gathered around the sanctum of Subramanya. Before the shrine stands the Garuda Stambha, a pillar sheathed in silver, which tradition holds shields devotees from the venom flung by the breath of Vasuki, who dwells within. Devotees approach the sanctum by passing behind this pillar, and the temple's setting in the forested ghats is part of its power.
sections.legends: Tradition tells that after Kartikeya slew the demon Tarakasura, he came to the Kumaradhara and there received the worship of Vasuki, the serpent king, who had taken refuge with him fearing the eagle Garuda. Subramanya granted the serpents his protection, and so the lord and the snake-king are worshipped together — the reason the temple is sought above all others for remedy of the serpent-curse.
sections.festivals: The great festival is the Champa Shashti (Subramanya Shashti) in the month of Margashira, when the deity is drawn in procession and the valley fills with pilgrims. Through the year the temple performs the serpent rites — Sarpa Samskara, Ashlesha Bali, and Naga Prathishtha — on scheduled days, for which devotees book far in advance.
sections.experience: Kukke draws pilgrims from across India carrying a single hope — release from the sarpa dosha — and the temple's rites and its setting among the river and the forested ghats give the visit a quiet gravity. It is a place approached with a petition, and left with a sense of burden lifted.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday break; special serpent-remedy rituals (Sarpa Samskara, Ashlesha Bali) are performed on scheduled days that must be booked. Confirm current timings and ritual dates before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Kukke Subramanya lies in Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka, in the Western Ghats on the Kumaradhara river; it is reached by road from Mangaluru and Bengaluru, with the nearest railheads at Subrahmanya Road and Mangaluru.
